architecture: Minimal TypeScript CLI with two concrete source files and no runtime dependencies. `src/index.ts` is the owned entry point: it reads `process.argv.slice(2)`, requires command `sum`, requires exactly two operands, delegates operand validation/formatting to the published `src/numeric.ts` interface via `import { parseOperand, formatSum } from './numeric.js'`, prints success as normalized numeric text plus `\n` to stdout, and writes helpful errors to stderr with non-zero exit. `src/numeric.ts` owns trimming and finite-decimal validation so both developers can start concurrently against the published interface. Direct execution sets `process.exitCode = main(process.argv.slice(2))`; any direct-execution guard must use `pathToFileURL` from `node:url`. Only Node built-ins are permitted; the numeric helper needs no imports. Normalization is end-to-end: operands are trimmed before validation, `1.0` normalizes to `1`, `" 1.0 "` normalizes to `1`, and output is `String(sum)` followed by a newline. Empty or whitespace-only operands are rejected after trimming.

tickets.title: CLI entry, command dispatch, stdout/stderr and exit behavior
tickets.description: Developer-a owns the CLI entry point only. Implement `src/index.ts` against the published `./numeric.js` interface. Enforce command `sum`, exactly two operands, trim/normalize via `parseOperand`, print successful normalized sum plus newline to stdout, return 0 on success, and return 1 with helpful stderr and no stdout for missing/unknown command, wrong operand count, or invalid operands. Use only Node built-ins and import the helper from the exact published path.

tickets.title: Numeric operand validation and normalized formatting helper
tickets.description: Developer-b owns the published numeric helper only. Implement `src/numeric.ts` with the exact `ParseOperandResult`, `parseOperand`, and `formatSum` signatures. `parseOperand` must trim first, reject empty/whitespace-only/non-numeric/NaN/Infinity values, accept finite decimal syntax, and return both numeric value and normalized `String(value)`. `formatSum` must return exact normalized numeric text. This ticket can start independently because its interface is published in the plan and developer-a codes against it without needing this file first.
